There is no reason why these kinds of arrangements cannot do well. Several multi-employer plans already exist, and they offer “administered funds,” rather than each employer having to sponsor its own separate account. These plans usually assume responsibility for core management functions, including the creation and upkeep of investment portfolios, as well as ensuring that administrative tasks are performed. Due to some risk involved, existing multiple-employer plans commonly set investment limits between $50 and $500 per employee, while the plan can handle unlimited capital.
